findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Under forced colors the selected segment is indistinguishable: selection is drawn only by the indicator fill, its shadow and a text-colour change, all of which forced colors replace.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/segmented-control/segmented-control.css has no @media (forced-colors) block; selection = indicator background/box-shadow (lines 164-185) + item colour (100-102, 198-200). packages/ui-react/src/styles/recipes.test.ts:363-378 documents that 'a state drawn by colour alone vanishes' and guards tabs and toggle-group, not segmented-control.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors block: `.a63-SegmentedControl-indicator { background-color: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none }` and `.a63-SegmentedControl-item[data-active] { color: HighlightText; forced-color-adjust: none }`; add 'segmented-control' to the it.each list in recipes.test.ts and a ForcedColors story/baseline like radio's.

verified.reason: segmented-control.css has no forced-colors block (grep finds none). Selection is drawn only by the indicator's background-color/box-shadow (indicator rule ~lines 164-185) and the [data-active] item colour. Forced colors replace both fills with Canvas, drop box-shadow and force the text to CanvasText, so the selected segment cannot be told apart. The focus outline appears only on :focus-visible. recipes.test.ts lines 363-378 guard tabs and toggle-group but not segmented-control, which is the same class of gap as the round-0 radio P1.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Rest props (including aria-label and aria-labelledby) are spread onto Tabs.Root, a role-less div, so the tablist cannot be given an accessible name.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:66-83 spreads {...props} on Tabs.Root; Base UI sets role='tablist' only on Tabs.List (node_modules/@base-ui/react/tabs/list/TabsList.js:91). segmented-control.test.tsx:97-113 asserts aria-label lands on the root div.
findings.fix: Forward aria-label / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby to Tabs.List (keep id, data-* and ref on the root), update the test to assert the tablist's name, and add a labelled example.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: In terminal/dark (neutral tone) the selected label is dimmer than the unselected labels, and the selected pill is a neutral grey on the navy track.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-segmentedcontrol-themes-chromium-linux.png terminal/dark row: lightest pixel of the selected 'List' label rgb(110,157,231) vs 'Grid' rgb(153,186,217); pill rgb(34,34,34) on track rgb(19,25,34). Provisional taste.
findings.fix: Set terminal dark --a63-segment-selected-foreground to a value at least as bright as --a63-segment-foreground (or the primary text), and give the selected background a navy-tinted surface; confirm on the contact sheet.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Segments use tab/tablist semantics with no tab panels, and every tab gets a title tooltip duplicating its visible label.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:83-93 (Tabs.Tab with aria-label and title = item.label even in the label variant). Screen readers announce 'tab, 1 of 3' with no panel to move to.
findings.fix: Decide whether a mode switch without panels should be a radiogroup or a toggle-group pattern; in any case drop `title` in the label variant (keep it only for icon-only segments).

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: The contract's disabled state has no story or visual baseline, and there is no RTL story.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.json:9 lists 'disabled'; grep 'disabled' in segmented-control.stories.tsx returns nothing; no segmentedcontrol-*disabled* or *right-to-left* baseline in apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/.
findings.fix: Add a States story (disabled segment, accent + neutral) and a RightToLeft story, and regenerate baselines.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Two boolean props (animateBackplate, fullWidth) and an items-array-only API; segments cannot carry custom content.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:25-32.
findings.fix: Keep for now; if the API is revisited, express layout as a `width` axis (auto | fill) in the contract and consider composable segment children.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Under forced colors the rail and the filled range disappear; only the thumb outline remains.
findings.evidence: slider.css:33-47: track and indicator are background fills with no border; no @media (forced-colors) block in slider.css; slider missing from recipes.test.ts:368-377.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors block: track gets `border: 1px solid CanvasText`, indicator `background-color: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none`; add 'slider' to the recipes.test.ts forced-colors list and a ForcedColors story.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: The unfilled rail is nearly invisible in every theme and mode (1.02-1.18:1 against the page), so the range extent and the remaining amount cannot be seen.
findings.evidence: Measured on ui-react-slider-themes-chromium-linux.png at x=270: modern light 1.11, modern dark 1.11, aqua light 1.18, aqua dark 1.02, retro light/dark 1.11, terminal light 1.18, terminal dark 1.05. Track = --a63-surface-muted (slider.css:38). Progress, using a border + field background (progress.css:29-31), stays visible.
findings.fix: Give the rail the progress treatment (hairline --a63-border-subtle border or a stronger fill) so it reaches at least 3:1 against the surface, and verify in the Themes baseline.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Slider's default tone is accent, while AGENTS.md rule 5 says to set tone="accent" on a Slider only when it is one of the view's one or two accent cues.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/slider.json:21 defaultTone 'accent'; slider.tsx:71; AGENTS.md rule 5. The same conflict applies to Progress (r1-k02-choice-14).
findings.fix: Either make `neutral` the contract default for Slider and Progress (matching SegmentedControl, whose default is neutral), or reword rule 5; regenerate contracts and baselines.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: The disabled state and a thumb hover state are not designed or captured.
findings.evidence: slider.json:8 lists 'disabled'; no disabled story (grep in slider.stories.tsx); slider.css has no :hover rule for the thumb.
findings.fix: Add a disabled example to a States story and a hover affordance on the thumb (gated by @media (hover: hover)).

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: The neutral tone fills with --a63-text-primary as a background (a craft-baseline token-role entry), and Progress does the same through a custom property that the check does not see.
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json:10 ('token-role | slider.css | background-color: var(--a63-text-primary)'); slider.css:49-51; progress.css:50-52 (--progress-fill: var(--a63-text-primary)).
findings.fix: Introduce or reuse a neutral solid token (e.g. --a63-action-neutral as Toggle does) for both fills and remove the baseline entry.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: In light mode the stars fail 3:1 non-text contrast: on stars 2.04:1 and off stars 1.64:1 against the page.
findings.evidence: Measured on ui-react-rating-themes-chromium-linux.png row 1: on rgb(243,159,0), off rgb(197,197,197), page rgb(249,249,249). --rating-on = --a63-category-amber (= --color-warning-500), --rating-off = text-secondary at 35% (rating.css:11-12).
findings.fix: Use a darker amber step (or the -subtle-foreground) for --rating-on in light mode and raise --rating-off, or outline off stars, so on/off reach 3:1 against the surface.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The input rating is controlled-only (value required, no defaultValue), and the radio rounds the value while the star fill does not.
findings.evidence: rating.tsx:10-23 (value: number required); rating.tsx:85 String(Math.round(value)) vs rating.tsx:92 data-on={star <= value}: value=2.5 checks radio 3 while only 2 stars are on.
findings.fix: Add defaultValue with internal state (useControlled-style), and derive data-on from the same rounded value used for the radio.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: Rating looks identical in all four themes, and its Themes story has no row labels and uneven rows.
findings.evidence: ui-react-rating-themes-chromium-linux.png: same amber lucide stars in all 8 rows, no theme/mode labels (other batch stories label rows), retro/light row taller than the others.
findings.fix: Decide whether rating expresses the theme archetype (e.g. retro bevel or terminal glyph) or stays a neutral content colour; at minimum label the Themes rows like checkbox/slider and even the row heights.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The hover preview is not gated by (hover: hover), so a tap leaves a sticky preview on touch devices.
findings.evidence: rating.css:83-88 (:has(.a63-Rating-item:hover) and :hover ~ rules outside any hover media query).
findings.fix: Wrap the two hover rules in @media (hover: hover).

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The arrow-key behaviour the contract promises is untested, and an input rating without `label` renders an unnamed radiogroup.
findings.evidence: rating.json:5 ('so arrow keys change the value'); rating.test.tsx has 3 cases, none keyboard; rating.tsx:79 aria-label={label} with label optional.
findings.fix: Add an ArrowRight/ArrowLeft test, and warn in development (or require label/aria-labelledby in types) for the input form.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: Progress's default tone is accent, while AGENTS.md rule 5 says to set tone="accent" on Progress only when it is one of the view's accent cues.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/progress.json:21 defaultTone 'accent'; progress.tsx:25; AGENTS.md rule 5. Same decision as r1-k02-choice-9.
findings.fix: Resolve together with r1-k02-choice-9: neutral default, or reword rule 5.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: The WithLabelAndValue example names the bar 'Example progress' with aria-label, overriding its visible ProgressLabel 'Downloading' (label in name mismatch).
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/progress/progress.stories.tsx:34-36; served verbatim by `pnpm -s atom63 example progress WithLabelAndValue`.
findings.fix: Drop aria-label from the composed example so ProgressLabel names the bar.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: The indeterminate sweep uses physical translateX, so it runs left-to-right in right-to-left layouts.
findings.evidence: progress.css:66-73.
findings.fix: Flip the keyframes under :dir(rtl) (e.g. a --progress-dir multiplier as switch.css does).

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: role=status sits on the svg with a static aria-label, which is not reliably announced on insertion and doubles up with visible loading text.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:30-34; spinner.stories.tsx:15-18 pairs <Spinner/> with visible 'Loading component data', so assistive tech gets 'Loading' plus the text.
findings.fix: Make the svg aria-hidden and render the status as a wrapping span role=status with visually hidden text from a `label` prop; let callers who show visible text pass label={null} / aria-hidden.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner has no exported props type and injects a <style> element into every instance instead of shipping a recipe in styles.css.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:5-25,39 (SPINNER_STYLE inside each svg); `pnpm -s atom63 component spinner` prints 'Types: None.'; spinner/ has no spinner.css unlike the other seven components.
findings.fix: Move the keyframes and class into spinner.css (bundled into styles.css), export `SpinnerProps`, and regenerate the API report.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner has no size axis; examples size it with inline pixel styles.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:15 fixed 1rem; spinner.stories.tsx:25-27 style={{ height: 12, width: 12 }} etc.; spinner.json has no sizes list.
findings.fix: Add a contract size axis tied to the control icon sizes (or document that it inherits 1em from the text), and update the Sizes story.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: The accessible name is hard-coded English 'Loading' with no label prop.
findings.evidence: spinner.tsx:30.
findings.fix: Add a `label` prop (default 'Loading') and document it; covered by the same change as r1-k02-choice-20.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: The CLI example for spinner imports from './spinner', so it does not run in a consumer app.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 example spinner Playground` output line 3: import { Spinner } from './spinner'; source spinner.stories.tsx:3.
findings.fix: Import from '@atom63/ui-react' in spinner.stories.tsx like the other stories, and regenerate the CLI index.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: Spinner has no Themes matrix and no visual archetype, so it is the same glyph in every theme.
findings.evidence: spinner.json:7 visualArchetypes []; spinner.stories.tsx:32-34 ('has no Themes matrix'); only playground/sizes/dark baselines.
findings.fix: Add a Themes story, then decide whether themes (e.g. terminal) express the spinner differently.

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: The reduced-motion still frame (a static quarter arc) is not captured or tested.
findings.evidence: spinner.json:6 lists 'reduced-motion'; spinner.tsx:20-24; no reduced-motion story or test.
findings.fix: Add a reduced-motion story/baseline and a test asserting animation: none.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: Checkbox and Switch have no forced-colors repaint; their checked state survives only through the icon or thumb position, and neither is in the forced-colors regression list.
findings.evidence: No forced-colors block in checkbox.css or switch.css; recipes.test.ts:368-377 lists radio but not checkbox or switch.
findings.fix: Repaint checked state with Highlight/HighlightText as radio.css:126-136 does, and add both to the recipes.test.ts list.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: The contract's invalid state is styled but never captured in a story or baseline.
findings.evidence: checkbox.json:8 'invalid'; checkbox.css:109-111; checkbox.stories.tsx States (lines 28-38) has no aria-invalid example (radio.stories.tsx:116 does).
findings.fix: Add an invalid checkbox to the States story and regenerate the baseline.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: Checkbox, Radio and Switch always fill with the brand accent and have no tone axis, while AGENTS.md rule 5 says 'Selection is neutral by default'.
findings.evidence: checkbox.css:11, radio.css:17, switch.css:28 (--a63-selection-accent -> --a63-action-primary); checkbox.mdx 'the checked fill is the brand primary'; AGENTS.md rule 5.
findings.fix: Decide whether rule 5's 'selection' excludes these form controls (then say so in the rule) or whether they get a neutral default.

findings.subject: radio
findings.summary: Radio stories teach duplicate option names and unnamed groups.
findings.evidence: radio.stories.tsx:107-116: two radios both named 'Example radio option', groups without aria-label (the conformance test does name its group).
findings.fix: Give each option a distinct name and each RadioGroup an aria-label in the stories.

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: The switch hover rule is not gated by (hover: hover), unlike checkbox and radio.
findings.evidence: switch.css:137-139 vs checkbox.css:94-98 and radio.css:96-100.
findings.fix: Wrap the hover rule in @media (hover: hover).

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: The thumb-icon example labels the state ('Dark appearance' / 'Light appearance') instead of the setting, against the component's own guidance.
findings.evidence: switch.stories.tsx:121 aria-label={checked ? 'Dark appearance' : 'Light appearance'}; `atom63 component switch` guidance: 'Label the setting rather than the state'.
findings.fix: Use a fixed label such as 'Dark appearance' and let aria-checked carry the state.
